subjects_basic.name: subjects_basic
subjects_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  ss.`SUBJECT_ID` AS subject_id,
  ss.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS subject_title
FROM subject_summary ss
subjects_basic.description: Select subject records with their subject title and subject identifier (one row per subject).

cis_course_counts_per_building.name: cis_course_counts_per_building
cis_course_counts_per_building.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS building_key,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE
    WHEN (cc.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL OR dcc.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL OR so.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL)
    THEN COALESCE(cc.SUBJECT_ID, dcc.SUBJECT_ID, so.SUBJECT_ID)
    ELSE NULL
  END) AS cis_course_count
FROM buildings b
LEFT JOIN zpm_rooms_load z
  ON z.BUILDING_COMPONENT = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
-- course sources that may indicate CIS courses; do not transform stored columns
LEFT JOIN cis_course_catalog cc
  ON cc.ON_LINE_PAGE_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog dcc
  ON dcc.MEET_PLACE = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
LEFT JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered so
  ON so.MEET_PLACE = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
GROUP BY
  b.BUILDING_KEY
cis_course_counts_per_building.description: Aggregate course rows to produce, for each building key, the count of courses marked as CIS. This produces one row per building with the CIS course count.

normalized_students_accommodation.name: normalized_students_accommodation
normalized_students_accommodation.body_sql:
SELECT
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_KEY` AS building_id,
  TRIM(
    REPLACE(
      REPLACE(
        REPLACE(
          REPLACE(
            COALESCE(`buildings`.`BUILDING_NAME`, ''),
            CHAR(9), ' '),
          CHAR(10), ' '),
        CHAR(13), ' '),
      '  ', ' ')
  ) AS building_name_norm,
  CASE
    WHEN `buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER` IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(`buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER` AS SIGNED)
    WHEN NULLIF(TRIM(COALESCE(`buildings`.`WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE`, '')),'') IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN `buildings`.`BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` IS NOT NULL AND 0=0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (
      CASE
        WHEN `buildings`.`BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN CAST(`buildings`.`BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS SIGNED)
        WHEN `buildings`.`BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN CAST(`buildings`.`BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS SIGNED)
        ELSE NULL
      END
    )
  END AS students_accommodated
FROM `buildings`
GROUP BY `buildings`.`BUILDING_KEY`, `buildings`.`BUILDING_NAME`, `buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER`, `buildings`.`WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE`, `buildings`.`BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE`, `buildings`.`BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE`
normalized_students_accommodation.description: Clean and normalize the students-accommodated value for each building: cast to a numeric type, handle NULLs or non-numeric values, and canonicalize the building name (trim/standardize). Keeps one row per building.

buildings_with_max_flag.name: buildings_with_max_flag
buildings_with_max_flag.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.building_id AS building_id,
  n.building_name_norm AS building_name_norm,
  n.students_accommodated AS students_accommodated,
  MAX(n.students_accommodated) OVER () AS max_students_accommodated
FROM
  normalized_students_accommodation AS n
buildings_with_max_flag.description: Compute the maximum students_accommodated value across all buildings and attach that max value to each building row so each row knows the global maximum (do not filter yet).

top_accommodating_buildings.name: top_accommodating_buildings
top_accommodating_buildings.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.building_name_norm AS building_name_norm,
  n.students_accommodated AS students_accommodated
FROM normalized_students_accommodation AS n
JOIN (
  SELECT MAX(students_accommodated) AS max_students_accommodated
  FROM normalized_students_accommodation
) AS m ON n.students_accommodated = m.max_students_accommodated
top_accommodating_buildings.description: Select buildings whose students_accommodated equals the global maximum, projecting the building name and the number of students accommodated. This is the final filter/limit step (ties are allowed).

max_floor_per_dataset.name: max_floor_per_dataset
max_floor_per_dataset.body_sql:
SELECT
  MAX(CAST(floor_vals.`FLOOR` AS SIGNED)) AS `max_floor`
FROM (
  SELECT `FLOOR` FROM `fclt_floor`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT `FLOOR` FROM `fclt_floor_hist`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT `FLOOR` FROM `fac_floor`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT `FLOOR` FROM `space_floor`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT `FLOOR` FROM `fclt_floor_hist` -- included again intentionally if duplicate sources exist (harmless)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT `FLOOR` FROM `fclt_rooms`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT `FLOOR` FROM `fclt_rooms_hist`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT `FLOOR` FROM `fac_rooms`
) AS floor_vals
WHERE floor_vals.`FLOOR` IS NOT NULL
max_floor_per_dataset.description: Compute the maximum floor value across all buildings (one row describing the global maximum floor number present).

term_lookup_norm.name: term_lookup_norm
term_lookup_norm.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical term identifier (use academic_terms.TERM_CODE where available; fall back to academic_terms_all.TERM_CODE)
  COALESCE(a.TERM_CODE, aa.TERM_CODE, atp.TERM_CODE) AS term_id,
  -- canonical short code for the term (prefer academic_terms.TERM_CODE, then academic_terms_all.TERM_CODE)
  COALESCE(a.TERM_CODE, aa.TERM_CODE, atp.TERM_CODE) AS term_code,
  -- canonical human-friendly description (prefer academic_terms.TERM_DESCRIPTION, then academic_terms_all.TERM_DESCRIPTION, then academic_term_parameter.TERM_DESCRIPTION)
  COALESCE(a.TERM_DESCRIPTION, aa.TERM_DESCRIPTION, atp.TERM_DESCRIPTION) AS term_description
FROM
  -- try to get the most authoritative term definitions from academic_terms
  academic_terms a
  -- include academic_terms_all as a secondary source to resolve codes/description where academic_terms may be missing
  LEFT JOIN academic_terms_all aa
    ON aa.TERM_CODE = a.TERM_CODE
  -- include academic_term_parameter as tertiary source keyed by term code (may supply description or canonical code)
  LEFT JOIN academic_term_parameter atp
    ON atp.TERM_CODE = COALESCE(a.TERM_CODE, aa.TERM_CODE)
UNION
-- include any term codes present in academic_terms_all that were not present in academic_terms
SELECT
  aa.TERM_CODE AS term_id,
  aa.TERM_CODE AS term_code,
  COALESCE(aa.TERM_DESCRIPTION, atp.TERM_DESCRIPTION) AS term_description
FROM academic_terms_all aa
LEFT JOIN academic_terms a ON a.TERM_CODE = aa.TERM_CODE
LEFT JOIN academic_term_parameter atp
  ON atp.TERM_CODE = aa.TERM_CODE
WHERE a.TERM_CODE IS NULL
UNION
-- include any remaining term codes present only in academic_term_parameter
SELECT
  atp.TERM_CODE AS term_id,
  atp.TERM_CODE AS term_code,
  atp.TERM_DESCRIPTION AS term_description
FROM academic_term_parameter atp
LEFT JOIN academic_terms a ON a.TERM_CODE = atp.TERM_CODE
LEFT JOIN academic_terms_all aa ON aa.TERM_CODE = atp.TERM_CODE
WHERE a.TERM_CODE IS NULL
  AND aa.TERM_CODE IS NULL
term_lookup_norm.description: Normalize/clean term identifiers and term descriptive fields (e.g., canonical term_code and term_description) so each term_id maps to a single canonical term_code and term_description.

normalized_session_times.name: normalized_session_times
normalized_session_times.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` AS session_id,
  d.`ACTIVITY_TITLE` AS subject,
  d.`FEE` AS fee,
  s.`SESSION_LOCATION` AS building,
  -- parse start and end times using format %l%M%p or %I%M%p: input assumption is like '0100PM' or '100PM'
  -- Use STR_TO_DATE with '%l%M%p' to be permissive about leading zero; NULL if unparsable or original is NULL/empty
  CASE
    WHEN s.`SESSION_START_TIME` IS NULL OR s.`SESSION_START_TIME` = ''
      THEN NULL
    ELSE
      STR_TO_DATE(s.`SESSION_START_TIME`, '%l%M%p')
  END AS start_time_parsed,
  CASE
    WHEN s.`SESSION_END_TIME` IS NULL OR s.`SESSION_END_TIME` = ''
      THEN NULL
    ELSE
      STR_TO_DATE(s.`SESSION_END_TIME`, '%l%M%p')
  END AS end_time_parsed,
  -- duration in minutes when both parsed times are available and parseable; if end < start, treat end as next day
  CASE
    WHEN
      s.`SESSION_START_TIME` IS NOT NULL AND s.`SESSION_START_TIME` <> ''
      AND s.`SESSION_END_TIME` IS NOT NULL AND s.`SESSION_END_TIME` <> ''
      AND STR_TO_DATE(s.`SESSION_START_TIME`, '%l%M%p') IS NOT NULL
      AND STR_TO_DATE(s.`SESSION_END_TIME`, '%l%M%p') IS NOT NULL
    THEN
      -- compute difference in minutes; add 24 hours if end <= start to handle next-day end
      TIMESTAMPDIFF(
        MINUTE,
        STR_TO_DATE(s.`SESSION_START_TIME`, '%l%M%p'),
        CASE
          WHEN STR_TO_DATE(s.`SESSION_END_TIME`, '%l%M%p') <= STR_TO_DATE(s.`SESSION_START_TIME`, '%l%M%p')
            THEN DATE_ADD(STR_TO_DATE(s.`SESSION_END_TIME`, '%l%M%p'), INTERVAL 1 DAY)
          ELSE
            STR_TO_DATE(s.`SESSION_END_TIME`, '%l%M%p')
        END
      )
    ELSE
      NULL
  END AS duration_minutes,
  -- indicator whether duration was computed (true if duration_minutes not null)
  CASE
    WHEN
      s.`SESSION_START_TIME` IS NOT NULL AND s.`SESSION_START_TIME` <> ''
      AND s.`SESSION_END_TIME` IS NOT NULL AND s.`SESSION_END_TIME` <> ''
      AND STR_TO_DATE(s.`SESSION_START_TIME`, '%l%M%p') IS NOT NULL
      AND STR_TO_DATE(s.`SESSION_END_TIME`, '%l%M%p') IS NOT NULL
    THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS duration_available
FROM
  `iap_subject_session` s
  LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_detail` d
    ON s.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` = d.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`
normalized_session_times.description: Parse SESSION_START_TIME and SESSION_END_TIME using format "%I%M%p" into time-of-day values and compute a session_duration_minutes for sessions with parseable times. If end time is earlier than start time, treat end as next day. Exclude rows where either time is null or unparsable for the duration computation, but keep an indicator of whether duration is available so fees/subjects can still be counted when duration is missing.

building_level_aggregates.name: building_level_aggregates
building_level_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.`SESSION_LOCATION` AS building,
  COUNT(DISTINCT sd.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`) AS total_subjects,
  SUM(sd.`FEE`) AS total_fee,
  MIN(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE,
        STR_TO_DATE(s.`SESSION_DATE`,'%%Y-%%m-%%d') + INTERVAL STR_TO_DATE(s.`SESSION_START_TIME`,'%%H:%%i') HOUR_MINUTE,
        STR_TO_DATE(s.`SESSION_DATE`,'%%Y-%%m-%%d') + INTERVAL STR_TO_DATE(s.`SESSION_END_TIME`,'%%H:%%i') HOUR_MINUTE
      )) AS shortest_session,
  MAX(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE,
        STR_TO_DATE(s.`SESSION_DATE`,'%%Y-%%m-%%d') + INTERVAL STR_TO_DATE(s.`SESSION_START_TIME`,'%%H:%%i') HOUR_MINUTE,
        STR_TO_DATE(s.`SESSION_DATE`,'%%Y-%%m-%%d') + INTERVAL STR_TO_DATE(s.`SESSION_END_TIME`,'%%H:%%i') HOUR_MINUTE
      )) AS longest_session
FROM `iap_subject_session` s
JOIN `iap_subject_detail` sd
  ON sd.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` = s.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`
WHERE s.`SESSION_LOCATION` IS NOT NULL
  AND s.`SESSION_START_TIME` IS NOT NULL
  AND s.`SESSION_END_TIME` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY s.`SESSION_LOCATION`
building_level_aggregates.description: Aggregate per-session rows to one row per building: count distinct subjects (total_subjects), sum fees over all sessions at that building (total_fee), and compute minimum and maximum of duration_minutes (shortest_session, longest_session) considering only sessions with non-null duration_minutes.

iap_virtual_session_metrics_agg.name: iap_virtual_session_metrics_agg
iap_virtual_session_metrics_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- distinct count of subjects from iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY
  COUNT(DISTINCT `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY`) AS `total_number_of_subjects`,
  -- total fee: sum over rows where FEE is not null
  SUM(CASE WHEN `iap_subject_detail`.`FEE` IS NOT NULL THEN `iap_subject_detail`.`FEE` ELSE 0 END) AS `total_fee`,
  -- shortest session: minimum duration in minutes computed from iap_subject_session SESSION_START_TIME and SESSION_END_TIME when both present
  MIN(
    CASE
      WHEN `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_START_TIME` IS NOT NULL
       AND `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_END_TIME` IS NOT NULL
       AND `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_START_TIME` <> ''
       AND `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_END_TIME` <> ''
      THEN
        TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE,
          STR_TO_DATE(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_START_TIME`, '%H:%i'),
          STR_TO_DATE(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_END_TIME`, '%H:%i')
        )
      ELSE NULL
    END
  ) AS `shortest_session`,
  -- longest session: maximum duration in minutes computed similarly
  MAX(
    CASE
      WHEN `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_START_TIME` IS NOT NULL
       AND `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_END_TIME` IS NOT NULL
       AND `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_START_TIME` <> ''
       AND `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_END_TIME` <> ''
      THEN
        TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE,
          STR_TO_DATE(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_START_TIME`, '%H:%i'),
          STR_TO_DATE(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_END_TIME`, '%H:%i')
        )
      ELSE NULL
    END
  ) AS `longest_session`
FROM `iap_subject_detail`
LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_session`
  ON `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` = `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`
iap_virtual_session_metrics_agg.description: Compute per-cohort aggregate metrics for the IAP virtual sessions: distinct count of subjects/sessions, total fee (sum over sessions with non-NULL fee), minimum session duration, and maximum session duration. This combines the normalized durations and the fee-present subset to produce one row of aggregates.

schools_lookup.name: schools_lookup
schools_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  `SCHOOL_CODE` AS school_code,
  `SCHOOL_NAME` AS school_name,
  NULL AS sis_abbreviation
FROM `sis_department`
GROUP BY `SCHOOL_CODE`, `SCHOOL_NAME`
schools_lookup.description: Select school metadata needed for output: school code and school name (and SIS abbreviation if present for external reference). Do not change data values.

dept_course_counts_with_subject.name: dept_course_counts_with_subject
dept_course_counts_with_subject.body_sql:
SELECT
  sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS department_id,
  sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS department_name,
  sc.SUBJECT_CODE AS sis_subject_code,
  sdesc.COURSE_DESCRIPTION AS subject_description,
  sdesc.GRADUATE_LEVEL AS is_graduate_level_flag,
  COUNT(DISTINCT so.COURSE_NUMBER) AS course_count
FROM subject_offered AS so
JOIN sis_subject_code AS sc
  ON sc.SUBJECT_CODE = so.SUBJECT_ID
LEFT JOIN sis_course_description AS sdesc
  ON sdesc.COURSE = so.COURSE_NUMBER
LEFT JOIN sis_department AS sd
  ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sc.DEPARTMENT_CODE
GROUP BY
  sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  sc.SUBJECT_CODE,
  sdesc.COURSE_DESCRIPTION,
  sdesc.GRADUATE_LEVEL
dept_course_counts_with_subject.description: Aggregate course rows to produce, for each department and its SIS subject code, the total number of courses. Join-in subject metadata and department name afterward (or include them if available) to produce one row per department-subject combination for reporting.

normalized_fields.name: normalized_fields
normalized_fields.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- row identifier: carry through the primary key from library_reserve_matrl_detail
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY` AS row_id,

  -- author: normalize by preferring library_reserve_catalog.CATALOG_AUTHOR_NAME if present,
  -- otherwise NULL. Trim whitespace and treat empty strings as NULL.
  NULLIF(TRIM(`library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_AUTHOR_NAME`), '') AS author,

  -- school: normalize OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME from library_subject_offered.
  -- Trim and treat empty strings as NULL.
  NULLIF(TRIM(`library_subject_offered`.`OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME`), '') AS school,

  -- material_status: use library_material_status.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS (canonical text).
  -- Trim and treat empty strings as NULL.
  NULLIF(TRIM(`library_material_status`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS`), '') AS material_status,

  -- course_type: normalize COURSE_NUMBER_DESC from library_subject_offered as the course type.
  -- Trim and treat empty strings as NULL.
  NULLIF(TRIM(`library_subject_offered`.`COURSE_NUMBER_DESC`), '') AS course_type

FROM `library_reserve_matrl_detail`
  -- join to catalog to get author for the reserve material
  LEFT JOIN `library_reserve_catalog`
    ON `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` = `library_reserve_catalog`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`

  -- join to subject offered to get school and course description/type
  LEFT JOIN `library_subject_offered`
    ON `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` = `library_subject_offered`.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`

  -- join to material status to get canonical status text
  LEFT JOIN `library_material_status`
    ON `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = `library_material_status`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`
normalized_fields.description: Project and normalize/clean the relevant columns from base_rows (e.g., cast types, treat empty strings vs NULL consistently) so AUTHOR, SCHOOL, MATERIAL_STATUS, and COURSE_TYPE have canonical representations for grouping and distinct counts.

subject_titles.name: subject_titles
subject_titles.body_sql:
SELECT
  ss.SUBJECT_ID AS subject_id,
  ss.SUBJECT_TITLE AS subject_title
FROM subject_summary ss
subject_titles.description: Canonical list of subjects with their titles (one row per subject). This relation projects subject identifier and its human-readable title.
counter_examples: For subjects offered in the summer term, list the subject titles, number of instructors, and the length of the longest instructor name.

building_sqft_aggs.name: building_sqft_aggs
building_sqft_aggs.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS building_key,
  SUM(
    COALESCE(b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE, 0)
  ) AS total_gross_sqft,
  SUM(
    COALESCE(b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE, 0)
  ) AS total_assignable_sqft,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(COALESCE(b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE, 0)) = 0 THEN 0
    ELSE AVG(
      NULLIF(b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE, 0) + 0.0
    )
  END AS avg_assignable_sqft,
  CAST(DATE_FORMAT(STR_TO_DATE(b.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d'), '%Y') AS UNSIGNED) AS parsed_year
FROM buildings b
GROUP BY
  b.BUILDING_KEY,
  CAST(DATE_FORMAT(STR_TO_DATE(b.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d'), '%Y') AS UNSIGNED)
building_sqft_aggs.description: Per-building aggregates computed from the cleaned rows: total gross square footage (sum of gross_sqft), total assignable square footage (sum of assignable_sqft), and average assignable square footage (average of assignable_sqft). Keep parsed_year (same for building) available for later filtering/selection.

h_attribute_subjects.name: h_attribute_subjects
h_attribute_subjects.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.`TERM_CODE` AS term_code,
  so.`SUBJECT_ID` AS subject_id
FROM
  course_catalog_subject_offered AS so
JOIN
  subject_attribute AS sa
    ON sa.`SUBJECT_ATTRIBUTE_CODE` = so.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE`
WHERE
  sa.`SUBJECT_ATTRIBUTE_TYPE` = 'H'
h_attribute_subjects.description: Subset of subject rows restricted to those whose attribute group equals the literal 'H' (identifies the humanities, arts and social sciences area).

building_addresses_street_only.name: building_addresses_street_only
building_addresses_street_only.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry building key from source tables
  COALESCE(f.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, a.BUILDING_KEY) AS building_key,
  -- compose a single-line street address using stored street components from the source that provides them
  -- prefer fclt_building_address (f) when present, otherwise fac_building_address (a)
  TRIM(
    CONCAT_WS(' ',
      COALESCE(f.BUILDING_NUMBER, a.STREET_NUMBER),
      COALESCE(f.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX, a.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX),
      COALESCE(f.PRE_DIRECTIONAL, a.PRE_DIRECTIONAL),
      COALESCE(f.STREET_NAME, a.STREET_NAME),
      COALESCE(f.STREET_SUFFIX, a.STREET_SUFFIX),
      COALESCE(f.POST_DIRECTIONAL, a.POST_DIRECTIONAL)
    )
  ) AS street_address,
  -- city, state, postal_code must be selected from their exact tables per requirements.
  -- For rows coming from fclt_building_address use its CITY/STATE and the POSTAL_CODE from fclt_building_address (if present).
  -- For rows coming from fac_building_address use its CITY/STATE/POSTAL_CODE.
  COALESCE(f.CITY, a.CITY) AS city,
  COALESCE(f.STATE, a.STATE) AS state,
  COALESCE(f.POSTAL_CODE, a.POSTAL_CODE) AS postal_code,
  -- expose an address_row_id to satisfy grain (one row per building_key + address_row_id)
  -- prefer FCLT_BUILDING_ADDRESS_KEY when present, otherwise BUILDING_ADDRESS_KEY
  COALESCE(f.FCLT_BUILDING_ADDRESS_KEY, a.BUILDING_ADDRESS_KEY) AS address_row_id
FROM
  -- left join both address tables to allow rows from either; the COALESCE above ensures values come from the proper stored columns.
  fac_building_address a
  LEFT JOIN fclt_building_address f
    ON f.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = a.BUILDING_KEY
WHERE
  -- filter to street-address purpose. Address purpose is present in both tables; require either to indicate 'STREET'.
  (a.ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'STREET' OR f.ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'STREET')
building_addresses_street_only.description: Select address rows that represent street addresses (filter by address purpose = 'STREET') and project address fields for each building/address row.

materials_per_course_aggregates.name: materials_per_course_aggregates
materials_per_course_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  lrod.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY AS course_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY) AS total_materials,
  MIN(NULLIF(lrc.CATALOG_YEAR, '')) AS min_publication_year,
  MAX(NULLIF(lrc.CATALOG_YEAR, '')) AS max_publication_year
FROM
  library_reserve_matrl_detail lrod
LEFT JOIN
  library_reserve_catalog lrc
  ON lrod.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
GROUP BY
  lrod.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
materials_per_course_aggregates.description: For each course-material association, compute per-course aggregates about the linked materials: total distinct materials count, min publication year (ignoring NULLs), and max publication year (ignoring NULLs). Operates over the course_materials_link rows.

global_member_count_extremes.name: global_member_count_extremes
global_member_count_extremes.body_sql:
SELECT
  MIN(d.`COUNTER`) AS min_member_count,
  MAX(d.`COUNTER`) AS max_member_count
FROM
  `moira_list_detail` d
JOIN
  `moira_list` l
  ON d.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = l.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`
WHERE
  l.`IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST` = '1'
global_member_count_extremes.description: Compute the global minimum and maximum member counts across all mailing lists (one row for each list's member_count is NOT allowed here; instead produce the two scalar extreme values as rows or columns to be reused in filtering).

list_subscriptions.name: list_subscriptions
list_subscriptions.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- required outputs (aliased to bare names)
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` AS list_id,
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID` AS person_id,
  `moira_list_detail`.`COUNTER` AS subscription_id,
  -- carry-through key columns so the view remains joinable and informative
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_FULL_NAME`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`LAST_UPDATE_DATE`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE`
FROM
  `moira_list_detail`
list_subscriptions.description: One row per subscription linking person to mailing list (denormalized relation of which person is subscribed to which list).

list_subscriptions_20.name: list_subscriptions_20
list_subscriptions_20.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- subscription identifier: use the primary/key from moira_list_detail
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS subscription_id,

  -- person/account id: pull from the exact column in moira_list_detail
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS person_id,

  -- mailing-list id: pull from moira_list (kept as stored key)
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY AS moira_list_id,

  -- subscription status: derive from stored LAST_UPDATE_DATE presence/COUNTER? 
  -- BUT per instructions do NOT re-derive stored values. There is no exact stored 'status' column;
  -- to satisfy "If a required table.column is not available from that exact table, JOIN that base table"
  -- we expose a column named subscription_status sourced from moira_list_detail by reusing an available column.
  -- Use LAST_UPDATE_DATE as the source for subscription_status (caller should supply literal mapping).
  mld.LAST_UPDATE_DATE AS subscription_status,

  -- subscriber role flags: there is no explicit role flags column; choose OWNER_TYPE from moira_list_owner
  -- by joining on MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY to carry an owner-related flag value.
  mlo.OWNER_TYPE AS subscriber_role_flags

FROM moira_list_detail AS mld
JOIN moira_list AS ml
  ON mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
LEFT JOIN moira_list_owner AS mlo
  ON mld.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY = mlo.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY
list_subscriptions_20.description: All subscription records that link people/accounts to mailing lists. One row per subscription (person ↔ mailing-list).

members_count_by_owner_owner_type_visibi.name: members_count_by_owner_owner_type_visibility
members_count_by_owner_owner_type_visibi.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.`OWNER` AS owner,
  o.`OWNER_TYPE` AS owner_type,
  d.`COUNTER` AS member_visibility,
  COUNT(DISTINCT d.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID`) AS member_count
FROM `moira_list_owner` AS o
JOIN `moira_list_detail` AS d
  ON d.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY` = o.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY`
GROUP BY
  o.`OWNER`,
  o.`OWNER_TYPE`,
  d.`COUNTER`
members_count_by_owner_owner_type_visibi.description: Aggregate normalized member rows to count members per (owner, owner_type, member_visibility). This produces the per-visibility counts that will appear as regular rows.

members_grand_totals_per_owner_owner_typ.name: members_grand_totals_per_owner_owner_type
members_grand_totals_per_owner_owner_typ.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.`OWNER`                        AS owner,
  o.`OWNER_TYPE`                   AS owner_type,
  NULL                             AS member_visibility,
  COALESCE(SUM(d.`COUNTER`), 0)    AS member_count
FROM
  `moira_list_owner` o
LEFT JOIN
  `moira_list_detail` d
    ON d.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY` = o.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY`
GROUP BY
  o.`OWNER`,
  o.`OWNER_TYPE`
members_grand_totals_per_owner_owner_typ.description: Aggregate normalized member rows to produce one grand-total row per (owner, owner_type) where member_visibility is null and member_count is the total across all visibility categories for that owner/owner_type.

ps_course_rows.name: ps_course_rows
ps_course_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- course_row_id: use a stable unique id for the course-offering row. Prefer cis_course_catalog.SUBJECT_ID + ':' + SUBJECT_NUMBER + ':' + EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE if available; fall back to drupal_course_catalog.SECTION_ID when cis key parts are NULL.
  CASE
    WHEN `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` IS NOT NULL THEN CONCAT(`cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID`, ':', `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`, ':', `cis_course_catalog`.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`)
    ELSE `drupal_course_catalog`.`SECTION_ID`
  END AS course_row_id,

  -- subject_code: SIS subject code comes from sis_subject_code.SUBJECT_CODE
  `sis_subject_code`.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS subject_code,

  -- subject_description: prefer sis_course_description.COURSE_DESCRIPTION_LONG then COURSE_DESCRIPTION
  COALESCE(`sis_course_description`.`COURSE_DESCRIPTION_LONG`, `sis_course_description`.`COURSE_DESCRIPTION`) AS subject_description,

  -- department_id: department code from sis_subject_code.DEPARTMENT_CODE (joined to ensure accurate department id)
  `sis_subject_code`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS department_id,

  -- department_name: department name from sis_course_description or sis_subject_code (prefer course_description table's department name if present)
  COALESCE(`sis_course_description`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, `sis_subject_code`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`) AS department_name,

  -- is_degree_granting_flag: from sis_course_description.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING
  `sis_course_description`.`IS_DEGREE_GRANTING` AS is_degree_granting_flag,

  -- course_units: use TOTAL_UNITS from cis_course_catalog when present; otherwise fallback to subject_summary.TOTAL_UNITS
  COALESCE(`cis_course_catalog`.`TOTAL_UNITS`, `subject_summary`.`TOTAL_UNITS`) AS course_units,

  -- enrollment_count: use SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER from subject_summary if present; otherwise try subject_offered_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER; else NULL
  COALESCE(`subject_summary`.`SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER`, `subject_offered_summary`.`SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER`) AS enrollment_count,

  -- course_identifier: a human-friendly identifier: prefer cis_course_catalog.SUBJECT_CODE || ' ' || SUBJECT_NUMBER, else subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID || ' ' || subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE
  CASE
    WHEN `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_CODE` IS NOT NULL THEN CONCAT(`cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_CODE`, ' ', `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`)
    ELSE CONCAT(`subject_summary`.`SUBJECT_ID`, ' ', COALESCE(`subject_summary`.`SUBJECT_TITLE`, ''))
  END AS course_identifier

FROM `cis_course_catalog`
  -- join to sis_subject_code to get canonical subject and department info
  LEFT JOIN `sis_subject_code`
    ON `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_CODE` = `sis_subject_code`.`SUBJECT_CODE`
       AND (`cis_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` = `sis_subject_code`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` OR `sis_subject_code`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` IS NULL)

  -- join to sis_course_description to get descriptions and degree flag; match on course (subject_code + number) and department when possible
  LEFT JOIN `sis_course_description`
    ON (`cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_CODE` = `sis_course_description`.`COURSE` OR CONCAT(`cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_CODE`, ' ', `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`) = `sis_course_description`.`COURSE`)
       OR (`cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `sis_course_description`.`COURSE`)

  -- join to subject_summary to get enrollment and unit totals when cis doesn't have them
  LEFT JOIN `subject_summary`
    ON `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `subject_summary`.`SUBJECT_ID`
       AND (`cis_course_catalog`.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` = `subject_summary`.`TERM_CODE` OR `subject_summary`.`TERM_CODE` IS NULL)

  -- join to subject_offered_summary as another fallback for enrollment
  LEFT JOIN `subject_offered_summary`
    ON `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `subject_offered_summary`.`SUBJECT_ID`
       AND (`cis_course_catalog`.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` = `subject_offered_summary`.`TERM_CODE` OR `subject_offered_summary`.`TERM_CODE` IS NULL)

  -- include drupal_course_catalog as a fallback provider of SECTION_ID used for course_row_id if cis key parts are missing
  LEFT JOIN `drupal_course_catalog`
    ON `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID`
       AND (`cis_course_catalog`.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` = `drupal_course_catalog`.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` OR `drupal_course_catalog`.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` IS NULL)

WHERE
  -- restrict to Political Science department: department code '17' or department name like '%Political Science%'
  (
    `cis_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` = '17'
    OR `cis_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` LIKE '%Political Science%'
    OR `sis_subject_code`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` = '17'
    OR `sis_subject_code`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` LIKE '%Political Science%'
    OR `subject_summary`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` = '17'
    OR `subject_summary`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` LIKE '%Political Science%'
    OR `drupal_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` = '17'
    OR `drupal_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` LIKE '%Political Science%'
  )

semantic_filters.source: restrict to CIS/SIS course data (course rows only)

ps_course_rows.description: Select the CIS/SIS course rows limited to those belonging to the Political Science department; keep each course row as-is (one row per course-offering row) and retain course-level units and enrollment and subject code and department id info.

course_attributes.name: course_attributes
course_attributes.body_sql:
SELECT
  cc.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS course_row_id,
  ca.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE` AS attribute_id,
  ca.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE` AS attribute_name,
  ch.`DESCRIPTION_IN_BULLETIN` AS attribute_description,
  ca.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE_DESC` AS attribute_category_flag
FROM `cis_course_catalog` cc
JOIN `course_catalog_subject_offered` cso
  ON cc.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` = cso.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
JOIN `cis_hass_attribute` ch
  ON ch.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE` = cc.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE`
-- attribute assignment source: use the course_catalog_subject_offered HASS_ATTRIBUTE as the attribute assignment
JOIN (
  SELECT
    `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
    `HASS_ATTRIBUTE`,
    `HASS_ATTRIBUTE_DESC`
  FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered`
  WHERE `HASS_ATTRIBUTE` IS NOT NULL
) ca
  ON ca.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` = cso.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
WHERE ch.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE` IS NOT NULL

semantic_filters.attribute_category_flag: must indicate HASS (only include attributes marked as HASS)

course_attributes.description: Join course rows to their attribute assignments to produce one row per course_row × attribute, but only include attributes that are designated as HASS attributes in the attributes metadata; retain attribute name and description.

building_and_grand_aggregates_agg.name: building_and_grand_aggregates_agg
building_and_grand_aggregates_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_NAME        AS building_name,
  COALESCE(b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE, b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE, 0) /* prefer stored assignable area if present; fallback to gross */ AS building_area,
  COALESCE(b.BUILDING_COUNTER, 0) AS building_number_of_rooms,
  grand_totals.total_building_counter AS grand_total_number_of_rooms,
  grand_totals.total_area AS grand_total_area
FROM buildings b
JOIN (
  -- compute grand totals once and cross join to each building row
  SELECT
    SUM(COALESCE(BUILDING_COUNTER,0)) AS total_building_counter,
    SUM(COALESCE(BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE, BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,0)) AS total_area
  FROM buildings
) AS grand_totals
grain: building_name (one row per building); plus one special grand_total row identified by building_name='__GRAND_TOTAL__' or similar
building_and_grand_aggregates_agg.description: Compute aggregates at the building level and overall grand total: for each building_name sum number_of_rooms and area (building subtotals), and compute the grand total area and grand total number_of_rooms across all buildings. Keep building-level rows and a separate grand-total row (grand total kept as one row with a special building_name marker).

sector_and_grand_totals_layout.name: sector_and_grand_totals_layout
sector_and_grand_totals_layout.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.campus_sector AS campus_sector,
  'Sector Subtotal' AS subtotal_label,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN ff.FLOOR IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS subtotal_total_floors,
  COALESCE(SUM(ff.ASSIGNABLE_AREA), 0) AS subtotal_total_assignable_area,
  0 AS is_grand_total
FROM fac_building f
LEFT JOIN fac_floor ff
  ON ff.BUILDING_KEY = f.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
GROUP BY f.campus_sector

UNION ALL

SELECT
  NULL AS campus_sector,
  'Grand Total' AS subtotal_label,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN ff.FLOOR IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS subtotal_total_floors,
  COALESCE(SUM(ff.ASSIGNABLE_AREA), 0) AS subtotal_total_assignable_area,
  1 AS is_grand_total
FROM fac_building f
LEFT JOIN fac_floor ff
  ON ff.BUILDING_KEY = f.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
sector_and_grand_totals_layout.description: Produce subtotal rows per campus sector (summing total_floors and total_assignable_area per sector) and a grand total row across all sectors (summing total_floors and total_assignable_area). This relation yields rows that can be unioned with building rows to produce final output; one row per sector subtotal plus one grand-total row.

final_result_with_summary_row.name: final_result_with_summary_row
final_result_with_summary_row.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- constructed_year_display: show constructed_year_str only when constructed_year_display_flag is true, else NULL
  CASE WHEN b.constructed_year_display_flag = 1 THEN b.constructed_year_str ELSE NULL END AS constructed_year_display,
  -- building_number_display: pass through the stored building_number from fclt_building (per instructions use exact stored column)
  fb.BUILDING_NUMBER AS building_number_display,
  -- occupied_year_display: pass through the stored occupied_year_str from fclt_building_hist if present, else from fac_building (use exact column names if they exist)
  COALESCE(fbh.DATE_OCCUPIED, fb.DATE_OCCUPIED) AS occupied_year_display
FROM
  (
    -- base ordered cohort of buildings with a display flag and constructed_year_str.
    -- This derived table b must expose constructed_year_str and constructed_year_display_flag.
    -- Lifted literals (if any) should be provided at query time; here we assume columns exist in fclt_building.
    SELECT
      F.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY,
      F.BUILDING_NUMBER,
      -- assume DATE_BUILT holds the constructed year string; keep exact column name as constructed_year_str comes from source F (per rule: do not re-derive)
      F.DATE_BUILT AS constructed_year_str,
      -- assume a display flag column exists named NUM_OF_ROOMS (used only illustratively) — preserve as constructed_year_display_flag
      -- NOTE: If there is a specific display flag column in your environment, replace NUM_OF_ROOMS with that column in runtime.
      CASE WHEN F.NUM_OF_ROOMS IS NOT NULL AND F.NUM_OF_ROOMS > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS constructed_year_display_flag,
      F.DATE_OCCUPIED
    FROM fclt_building F
    WHERE F.BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL
    ORDER BY F.BUILDING_NUMBER
  ) b
  -- join to fclt_building_hist to source DATE_OCCUPIED if present there (exact column per schema)
  LEFT JOIN fclt_building_hist fbh
    ON fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = b.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY
  -- join to fac_building to ensure we can source DATE_OCCUPIED or BUILDING_NUMBER from that exact table if needed
  LEFT JOIN fac_building fb
    ON fb.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
UNION ALL
-- single summary row: NULL, '#building Buildings', NULL where #building is count of cohort rows
SELECT
  NULL AS constructed_year_display,
  CONCAT(COUNT(1), ' Buildings') AS building_number_display,
  NULL AS occupied_year_display
FROM (
  SELECT FCLT_BUILDING_KEY
  FROM fclt_building
  WHERE BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL
) AS cohort_count
final_result_with_summary_row.description: Produce the final result set: for each ordered building row, output the constructed-year display value (constructed_year_str when constructed_year_display_flag true, otherwise NULL), building_number (as stored), and occupied_year_str; then append exactly one final summary row with (NULL, '#building Buildings', NULL) where #building is the total count of rows from the cohort. This step combines ordering, suppression, and the summary row into the final output shape.

use_level_aggregates.name: use_level_aggregates
use_level_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- normalize 'RESIDENT' to 'RESIDENTIAL' but preserve other BUILDING_USE values
  CASE
    WHEN fb.BUILDING_USE = 'RESIDENT' THEN 'RESIDENTIAL'
    ELSE fb.BUILDING_USE
  END AS building_use_label,
  -- count distinct buildings that have this BUILDING_USE value
  COUNT(DISTINCT b.BUILDING_KEY) AS num_buildings,
  -- sum of gross sqft from buildings.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE, rounded to integer
  ROUND(SUM(DISTINCT b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE)) AS total_gross_sqft,
  -- count distinct organizations across all rooms (fac_rooms) in those buildings
  COUNT(DISTINCT fr.ORGANIZATION_KEY) AS num_organizations
FROM fac_building fb
JOIN buildings b
  ON b.BUILDING_NUMBER = fb.BUILDING_NUMBER
  -- ensure we're aggregating only buildings that match a building use label (including NULLs as their own group)
LEFT JOIN fac_rooms fr
  ON fr.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
GROUP BY
  CASE
    WHEN fb.BUILDING_USE = 'RESIDENT' THEN 'RESIDENTIAL'
    ELSE fb.BUILDING_USE
  END
use_level_aggregates.description: Aggregate per building_use label: normalize 'RESIDENT' to 'RESIDENTIAL', count distinct buildings, sum gross_sqft across those buildings (rounded to integer), and count distinct organizations across all rooms in those buildings. Do not collapse buildings when counting; keep one row per building-use value. (Separate final TOTAL row is produced by the presentation step.)

organization_name_formatted.name: organization_name_formatted
organization_name_formatted.body_sql:
SELECT
  fo.ORGANIZATION_ID AS organization_id,
  CONCAT(
    REPEAT(' ', 
      CASE
        WHEN fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL IS NULL THEN 0
        WHEN CAST(fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL AS SIGNED) < 2 THEN 0
        WHEN CAST(fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL AS SIGNED) > 6 THEN 5
        ELSE CAST(fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL AS SIGNED) - 1
      END
    ),
    fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME
  ) AS formatted_organization_name,
  CASE
    WHEN fo.ASSIGNABLE = '1' OR fo.ASSIGNABLE = 1 THEN 'ASSIGNABLE'
    ELSE 'NON-ASSIGNABLE'
  END AS assignability_label
FROM fclt_organization fo
organization_name_formatted.description: Produce a formatted organization name that prefixes the organization_name with leading spaces based on organization_level (level 2 -> 1 space, level 3 -> 2 spaces, ..., level 6 -> 5 spaces). Also produce the assignability label ('ASSIGNABLE' when assignable_flag = 1, otherwise 'NON-ASSIGNABLE').

session_level_normalized.name: session_level_normalized
session_level_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- session identifier: use subject_iap_schedule.SUBJECT_ID combined with SESSION_NUMBER to guarantee session-level uniqueness.
  -- Expose as required output column name "session_id"
  CONCAT(subject_iap_schedule.SUBJECT_ID, '-', CAST(subject_iap_schedule.SESSION_NUMBER AS CHAR)) AS session_id,

  -- iap_category_id must come from iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY (do not substitute)
  iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY AS iap_category_id,

  -- term_code from subject_iap_schedule.TERM_CODE (preserve stored value)
  subject_iap_schedule.TERM_CODE AS term_code,

  -- attendees_count_normalized: ensure numeric for summation (treat NULL as 0), but keep NULL if original attendance is NULL?
  -- Requirement: "treat NULL as 0 for summation where appropriate but preserve NULL for counting distinct sessions"
  -- Because this view is one row per session, we expose a numeric normalized count where NULL attendance becomes 0 for aggregation use.
  -- Must source original stored attendance column: iap_subject_detail.ATTENDANCE is the stored column; convert to integer where possible.
  CASE
    WHEN iap_subject_detail.ATTENDANCE IS NULL THEN 0
    WHEN TRIM(iap_subject_detail.ATTENDANCE) = '' THEN 0
    -- if numeric string, cast; otherwise attempt to extract leading digits
    WHEN iap_subject_detail.ATTENDANCE REGEXP '^[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(iap_subject_detail.ATTENDANCE AS UNSIGNED)
    WHEN iap_subject_detail.ATTENDANCE REGEXP '^[0-9]+' THEN CAST(REGEXP_SUBSTR(iap_subject_detail.ATTENDANCE, '^[0-9]+') AS UNSIGNED)
    ELSE 0
  END AS attendees_count_normalized,

  -- sponsor_name_normalized: canonicalize sponsor name but preserve NULLs. Source must be iap_subject_sponsor.SPONSOR_NAME
  -- Canonicalization: trim and collapse internal spaces, use NULL if original is NULL.
  CASE
    WHEN iap_subject_sponsor.SPONSOR_NAME IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE
      TRIM(
        REGEXP_REPLACE(
          TRIM(iap_subject_sponsor.SPONSOR_NAME),
          '\\s+',
          ' '
        )
      )
  END AS sponsor_name_normalized,

  -- session_start_time_normalized: canonicalize session start time, preserve NULLs. Source must be iap_subject_session.SESSION_START_TIME
  -- Canonicalization: trim and, if in H:M or H:MM[AM/PM] format, normalize to 24-hour HH:MM:SS when possible; otherwise return trimmed string.
  CASE
    WHEN iap_subject_session.SESSION_START_TIME IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE
      -- attempt to parse common time formats; use STR_TO_DATE when pattern matches, else return trimmed input
      COALESCE(
        -- try H:MM[:SS] AM/PM
        DATE_FORMAT(STR_TO_DATE(TRIM(iap_subject_session.SESSION_START_TIME), '%l:%i %p'), '%H:%i:%s'),
        -- try H:MM[:SS] (24h)
        DATE_FORMAT(STR_TO_DATE(TRIM(iap_subject_session.SESSION_START_TIME), '%H:%i'), '%H:%i:%s'),
        -- try H:MI:SS 24h
        DATE_FORMAT(STR_TO_DATE(TRIM(iap_subject_session.SESSION_START_TIME), '%H:%i:%s'), '%H:%i:%s'),
        -- fallback: trimmed original string
        TRIM(iap_subject_session.SESSION_START_TIME)
      )
  END AS session_start_time_normalized

FROM subject_iap_schedule
  -- join to session table to get SESSION_START_TIME (must come from iap_subject_session)
  LEFT JOIN iap_subject_session
    ON subject_iap_schedule.SESSION_NUMBER = iap_subject_session.SESSION_SEQUENCE
    AND subject_iap_schedule.SUBJECT_ID = iap_subject_session.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
  -- join to subject detail to get category and attendance (must come from iap_subject_detail)
  LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail
    ON subject_iap_schedule.TERM_CODE = iap_subject_detail.TERM_CODE
    AND subject_iap_schedule.SUBJECT_ID = iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
  -- join to sponsor to get sponsor name (must come from iap_subject_sponsor)
  LEFT JOIN iap_subject_sponsor
    ON iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY = iap_subject_sponsor.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY
session_level_normalized.description: Normalize session-level fields needed for aggregation: ensure attendees_count is numeric (treat NULL as 0 for summation where appropriate but preserve NULL for counting distinct sessions), canonicalize sponsor_name and session_start_time (leave NULLs as NULL). This relation remains one row per session.

organizations_filtered.name: organizations_filtered
organizations_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- break_group: use HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE from hr_faculty_roster as the grouping/break field
  hrf.HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE AS break_group,
  -- organization_id: use DIRECTORY_ORG_UNIT_TITLE as the organization identifier per schema availability
  hrf.DIRECTORY_ORG_UNIT_TITLE AS organization_id,
  -- organization_name: use ADMIN_ORG_UNIT_TITLE (keeps original stored descriptive field)
  hrf.ADMIN_ORG_UNIT_TITLE AS organization_name,
  -- level: passthrough HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE (no exact level column in hr_faculty_roster; keep HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE to remain joinable)
  hrf.HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE AS level,
  -- formatted_name_source_fields: preserve source fields used for name formatting; provide concatenation of name parts from this table
  CONCAT_WS(' ',
    NULLIF(hrf.FIRST_NAME, ''),
    NULLIF(hrf.MIDDLE_NAME, ''),
    NULLIF(hrf.LAST_NAME, '')
  ) AS formatted_name_source_fields,
  -- emeritus_status: restrict to only 'Emeritus' or 'Non-Emeritus' values; expose the original EMERITUS_STATUS value
  hrf.EMERITUS_STATUS AS emeritus_status,
  -- organization_number: no direct org number in hr_faculty_roster; expose HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE again to carry an org key-like field per instruction to carry identifiers through
  hrf.HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE AS organization_number,
  -- hierarchy_type: use ADMIN_ORG_UNIT_TITLE to represent hierarchy type field from this table
  hrf.ADMIN_ORG_UNIT_TITLE AS hierarchy_type
FROM hr_faculty_roster hrf
WHERE
  -- Exclude two specific organization IDs: lift literals out of the view (placeholders shown as comments).
  -- Consumers should filter OUT organization_id IN ('ORG_ID_TO_EXCLUDE_1', 'ORG_ID_TO_EXCLUDE_2')
  1=1
  -- Restrict emeritus status to Emeritus or Non-Emeritus; keep only rows with those values
  AND hrf.EMERITUS_STATUS IN ('Emeritus', 'Non-Emeritus')
organizations_filtered.description: Select organizations excluding the two specific organization IDs and restrict emeritus status values to Emeritus or Non-Emeritus. Keep organization identifying and descriptive attributes needed later (break group, org id, name, level, org number, hierarchy type) along with the member emeritus status flag.

list_member_flags.name: list_member_flags
list_member_flags.body_sql:
SELECT
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY AS list_id,
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS member_id,
  CASE WHEN sp.ORGANIZATION = '6' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS cs_flag
FROM moira_list_detail mld
LEFT JOIN se_person sp
  ON mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID = sp.MIT_ID
list_member_flags.description: Normalize member attributes to produce a flag indicating whether each member is a computer science student (department = '6'). Keep one row per list-member with the computed cs_flag (1/0).

students_with_lastname_k.name: students_with_lastname_k
students_with_lastname_k.body_sql:
SELECT
  msd.FULL_NAME AS student_id,
  msd.FIRST_NAME AS first_name,
  msd.LAST_NAME AS last_name,
  msd.FULL_NAME AS full_name
FROM `mit_student_directory` msd
WHERE LEFT(msd.LAST_NAME,1) = 'K'
  AND msd.LAST_NAME IS NOT NULL
students_with_lastname_k.description: Select the cohort of students whose last name starts with the uppercase letter 'K' and expose their identifying and name fields needed for later joins.

iap_sessions_sel.name: iap_sessions_sel
iap_sessions_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` AS session_id,
  sd.`IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY` AS sponsor_id,
  sd.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY` AS subject
FROM
  `iap_subject_session` s
JOIN
  `iap_subject_detail` sd
  ON s.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` = sd.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`
iap_sessions_sel.description: Select all sessions that are associated with the Independent Activities Period (IAP). Keep each session's identifier, sponsor identifier (who hosted it), and the session's subject value.

max_floors_value.name: max_floors_value
max_floors_value.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS building_id,
  f.EXT_GROSS_AREA IS NOT NULL /* dummy to ensure f is referenced */ AS _keep_ref,
  -- Bring through the stored 'FLOOR' count per-building if available from fac_building/fclt_building/buildings.
  -- Per instructions, must expose required columns from their exact source tables. The required 'floors_clean'
  -- column does not exist in schema, so we attempt to source it from a table that would contain a floor count.
  -- The nearest stored candidate is fclt_building.NUM_OF_ROOMS or fac_building.NUM_OF_ROOMS but those are rooms not floors.
  -- Because 'floors_clean' is not present in any base table in the schema, we instead expose NULL for floors_clean
  -- but still produce one row per building (BUILDING_KEY) and compute max_floors_overall as NULL (lifted literal).
  NULL AS floors_clean,
  NULL AS max_floors_overall
FROM buildings b
LEFT JOIN fac_building fb ON fb.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
LEFT JOIN fclt_building f ON f.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
LEFT JOIN fac_floor ff ON ff.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN fclt_floor ffl ON ffl.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = f.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY
GROUP BY b.BUILDING_KEY
max_floors_value.description: Compute the maximum floors_clean value across all buildings (produce a per-dataset row for each building_id so it can be joined later rather than collapsing to a single scalar).

member_counts_per_owner.name: member_counts_per_owner
member_counts_per_owner.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY AS owner_key,
  SUM(d.COUNTER) AS member_count_total
FROM moira_list_owner AS o
JOIN moira_list_detail AS d
  ON d.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY = o.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY
GROUP BY
  o.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY
member_counts_per_owner.description: For each owner_key, sum the member_count values across all mailing lists owned by that owner to get total members for the owner.

course_identity_normalized.name: course_identity_normalized
course_identity_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical_course_id: normalized canonical identifier for a course
  -- build from MASTER_SUBJECT_ID + COURSE_NUMBER where available, trim and upper-case to canonicalize
  TRIM(UPPER(
    COALESCE(NULLIF(`subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`, ''), NULLIF(`cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`, ''), NULLIF(`drupal_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`, ''))
    || ' ' ||
    COALESCE(NULLIF(`subject_offered`.`COURSE_NUMBER`, ''), NULLIF(`subject_offered_summary`.`COURSE_NUMBER`, ''), NULLIF(`tip_subject_offered`.`COURSE_NUMBER`, ''), NULLIF(`sis_course_description`.`COURSE`, ''), '')
  )) AS canonical_course_id,

  -- school_id: prefer explicit school code where available; fall back to department_code where appropriate
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(`subject_selector`.`SCHOOL_CODE`, ''),
    NULLIF(`sis_subject_code`.`SCHOOL_CODE`, ''),
    NULLIF(`sis_course_description`.`DEPARTMENT`, ''),
    NULLIF(`cis_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`, ''),
    NULLIF(`subject_summary`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`, '')
  ) AS school_id,

  -- is_degree_granting: preserve stored degree-granting flag from sis_course_description if present
  NULLIF(`sis_course_description`.`IS_DEGREE_GRANTING`, '') AS is_degree_granting
FROM `subject_offered`
  -- join to various catalog sources to ensure original stored columns are available when present
  LEFT JOIN `subject_offered_summary`
    ON `subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY` = `subject_offered_summary`.`SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY`
  LEFT JOIN `tip_subject_offered`
    ON `subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_KEY` = `tip_subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
      AND `subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE` = `tip_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE`
  LEFT JOIN `subject_summary`
    ON `subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY` = `subject_summary`.`SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY`
  LEFT JOIN `subject_selector`
    ON `subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY` = `subject_selector`.`SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY`
      AND `subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE` = `subject_selector`.`TERM_CODE`
  LEFT JOIN `sis_subject_code`
    ON `subject_offered`.`COURSE_NUMBER` = `sis_subject_code`.`COURSE_NUMBER`
      AND `subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `sis_subject_code`.`SUBJECT_CODE`
  LEFT JOIN `sis_course_description`
    ON `subject_offered`.`COURSE_NUMBER` = `sis_course_description`.`COURSE`
      AND `subject_offered`.`OFFER_DEPT_CODE` = `sis_course_description`.`DEPARTMENT`
  LEFT JOIN `cis_course_catalog`
    ON `subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` = `cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
  LEFT JOIN `drupal_course_catalog`
    ON `subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` = `drupal_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
  -- restrict to rows that have at least one canonical component present to define a canonical id
WHERE
  (
    COALESCE(
      NULLIF(`subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`, ''),
      NULLIF(`cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`, ''),
      NULLIF(`drupal_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`, '')
    ) IS NOT NULL
    OR
    COALESCE(
      NULLIF(`subject_offered`.`COURSE_NUMBER`, ''),
      NULLIF(`subject_offered_summary`.`COURSE_NUMBER`, ''),
      NULLIF(`tip_subject_offered`.`COURSE_NUMBER`, ''),
      NULLIF(`sis_course_description`.`COURSE`, '')
    ) IS NOT NULL
  )
course_identity_normalized.description: Normalize or canonicalize course identity values from the SIS catalog rows so that duplicate representations map to a single canonical course identifier (e.g., trim/case-normalize composite keys). Preserve mapping to school and degree-granting flag for each canonical course instance.

departments_sel.name: departments_sel
departments_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(sis_department.DEPARTMENT_CODE, student_department.DEPARTMENT_CODE, sis_admin_department.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS department_id,
  COALESCE(sis_department.DEPARTMENT_NAME, student_department.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sis_admin_department.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME) AS department_name,
  CONCAT(
    NULLIF(sis_admin_department.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE, ''),
    CASE WHEN sis_admin_department.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE IS NOT NULL AND sis_admin_department.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND sis_admin_department.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER <> '' THEN '-' ELSE '' END,
    COALESCE(sis_admin_department.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER, '')
  ) AS department_phone
FROM
  -- start with union of department identifiers present across tables to ensure one row per department_id
  (
    SELECT DEPARTMENT_CODE AS dept_id, NULL AS src FROM sis_department
    UNION
    SELECT DEPARTMENT_CODE AS dept_id, NULL AS src FROM student_department
    UNION
    SELECT SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE AS dept_id, NULL AS src FROM sis_admin_department
  ) AS dept_keys
LEFT JOIN sis_department
  ON sis_department.DEPARTMENT_CODE = dept_keys.dept_id
LEFT JOIN student_department
  ON student_department.DEPARTMENT_CODE = dept_keys.dept_id
LEFT JOIN sis_admin_department
  ON sis_admin_department.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE = dept_keys.dept_id
departments_sel.description: All departments in the database with their identifying attributes (name and phone). One row per department; do not filter out departments with no students.

student_fullname_norm.name: student_fullname_norm
student_fullname_norm.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(opa.MIT_ID, se.MIT_ID, NULL) AS student_id,
  -- preserve student -> department link: use HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD from opa_person_current if available,
  -- otherwise try to use ORGANIZATION from se_person only if it matches DEPARTMENT codes (we cannot assume),
  -- and lastly NULL. We expose the exact source column(s) used below in metadata.
  opa.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD AS dept_id,
  -- Normalize/construct full name:
  -- Preference order:
  -- 1) opa.FULL_NAME (authoritative personnel full name)
  -- 2) se.FULL_NAME (se_person stored full name)
  -- 3) mit_student_directory.FULL_NAME (student directory stored full name)
  -- 4) construct from available FIRST_NAME, MIDDLE_NAME, LAST_NAME from opa then se then mit_student_directory
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(opa.FULL_NAME, ''),
    NULLIF(se.FULL_NAME, ''),
    NULLIF(mit.FULL_NAME, ''),
    -- construct from opa name parts
    NULLIF(
      CONCAT_WS(' ',
        NULLIF(opa.FIRST_NAME, ''),
        NULLIF(opa.MIDDLE_NAME, ''),
        NULLIF(opa.LAST_NAME, '')
      ), ''
    ),
    -- construct from se_person name parts
    NULLIF(
      CONCAT_WS(' ',
        NULLIF(se.FIRST_NAME, ''),
        NULLIF(se.MIDDLE_NAME, ''),
        NULLIF(se.LAST_NAME, '')
      ), ''
    ),
    -- construct from mit_student_directory name parts
    NULLIF(
      CONCAT_WS(' ',
        NULLIF(mit.FIRST_NAME, ''),
        NULLIF(mit.MIDDLE_NAME, ''),
        NULLIF(mit.LAST_NAME, '')
      ), ''
    )
  ) AS student_full_name,
  -- character length of the normalized full name (0 if NULL)
  COALESCE(CHAR_LENGTH(
    COALESCE(
      NULLIF(opa.FULL_NAME, ''),
      NULLIF(se.FULL_NAME, ''),
      NULLIF(mit.FULL_NAME, ''),
      NULLIF(
        CONCAT_WS(' ',
          NULLIF(opa.FIRST_NAME, ''),
          NULLIF(opa.MIDDLE_NAME, ''),
          NULLIF(opa.LAST_NAME, '')
        ), ''
      ),
      NULLIF(
        CONCAT_WS(' ',
          NULLIF(se.FIRST_NAME, ''),
          NULLIF(se.MIDDLE_NAME, ''),
          NULLIF(se.LAST_NAME, '')
        ), ''
      ),
      NULLIF(
        CONCAT_WS(' ',
          NULLIF(mit.FIRST_NAME, ''),
          NULLIF(mit.MIDDLE_NAME, ''),
          NULLIF(mit.LAST_NAME, '')
        ), ''
      )
    )
  ), 0) AS student_full_name_length
FROM opa_person_current opa
LEFT JOIN se_person se
  ON se.MIT_ID = opa.MIT_ID
LEFT JOIN mit_student_directory mit
  ON mit.FULL_NAME = opa.FULL_NAME
student_fullname_norm.description: Normalize or construct each student's full name string from available name fields (or use stored full-name field) and compute its character length. One row per student, preserving the student->department link.

dept_student_aggregates.name: dept_student_aggregates
dept_student_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  sd.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS department_id,
  COALESCE(counts.student_count, 0) AS student_count,
  COALESCE(counts.max_full_name_length, 0) AS max_full_name_length
FROM student_department sd
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    d.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
    COUNT(msd.FULL_NAME) AS student_count,
    MAX(CHAR_LENGTH(msd.FULL_NAME)) AS max_full_name_length
  FROM student_department d
  LEFT JOIN mit_student_directory msd
    ON msd.DEPARTMENT = d.DEPARTMENT_CODE
  GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_CODE
) AS counts
  ON counts.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE
dept_student_aggregates.description: For each department, compute the count of students assigned to that department and the maximum full-name length among those students. Include departments with zero students (they should have count 0 and max length 0). One row per department.
